about.title: Personal Injury Help in Woodside, California
about.longDescription: Woodside's winding, rural character comes with its own traffic patterns. Public records show 42 injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, leaving 57 people hurt, with no reported traffic deaths. Corridors like Rt 84, Woodside Road, Portola Road, and La Honda Road see the highest volume of reported crashes, and Saturdays between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. tend to be the busiest window for collisions — likely tied to weekend traffic heading toward the coast and surrounding trails. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and next steps can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Woodside with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your situation. We are not a law firm, and we don't charge you anything to make the connection. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You focus on healing — let someone else worry about the paperwork and phone calls.

whyChoose.title: Why People in Woodside Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Connecting with an attorney early helps preserve evidence while it's still fresh.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help sort out how fault gets calculated in your case.

items.title: No Cap on What You May Recover
items.desc: Ordinary injury cases in California don't have a limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't artificially capped the way it might be in some other states.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you don't pay out of pocket to get started. Legal fees only come from a recovery, which means there's no upfront financial risk to finding out where you stand.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney. We are not a law firm, and there's no charge for making the connection.

items.question: What if I was partially at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't automatically bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how this might apply to your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If your claim involves a government entity, the window can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's wise not to delay.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Woodside?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along Rt 84, Woodside Road, Portola Road, and La Honda Road, with reported crashes tending to peak on Saturdays between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. This reflects neutral collision-count data, not a judgment about any specific road.

items.question: Will I owe attorney fees if I don't recover anything?
items.answer: No. Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, meaning fees only apply if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to you to explore your options.
